sentences.text: 6. Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is in jail since 16.09.2020.
It is argued that in the charge sheet total 19 witnesses have been shown by the prosecution out of whom only three witnesses have been examined in the trial.

Learned counsel has placed before the Court the statements of Awadhesh the first informant, was examined as P.W.-1, Om Prakash Prajapati the father of the deceased was examined as P.W.-2 and Chandra Prakash Mishra was examined as P.W.-3 and submitted that perusal of the same goes to show that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case inasmuch as the site plan and the version as given by the P.W.-3/Chandra Prakash Mishra is that the door of the room was bolted from inside and after breaking the same the deceased was found hanging and then the dead body was brought down.
It is argued that thus the same goes to show that the deceased committed suicide after bolting the door from inside.
It is argued that the applicant be released on bail.
7. Per contra, learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is husband of the deceased.
The first bail of the applicant was dismissed for want of prosecution and the second bail application was rejected on merits by this Court.
It is argued that in so far as the statements of the witnesses are concerned the same are to be considered by the trial court at the appropriate stage.
It is argued that the trial in the matter is going on and three (03) witnesses have been examined and release of the applicant at this stage may adversely affect the trial.
It is argued that hence the prayer for bail be rejected.
8. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the second bail application of the applicant was rejected by this Court on merits on 13.4.2022.

The said order reads as under:-
"Heard Sri Virendra Singh, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Sanjay Kumar Singh, learned AGA for the State and perused the material on record.

The second bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant Satish Seth @ Satish Soni, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 494 of 2020, under Sections 304B,
498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, registered at P.S. Shivpur, District Varanasi.
The first bail application being Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 2065 of 2021 was rejected by this Court vide order dated 13.1.2021 for want of prosecution.

sentences.text: Marriage was a love marriage solemnized around four years back.
When his sister came from her matrimonial house she told family members that her in-laws were saying that they were not given any dowry and they used to assault her.
There was demand of Rs. 1 lakh as dowry by the applicant and other co-accused persons.
On 10.09.2020 the first informant came to know that his sister has committed suicide by hanging herself.
She was living in a rented house in Bhawanipur, Shivpur.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
It is argued that the applicant is stated to be the husband of the deceased but the same is false.
The applicant never married the deceased.
The deceased after leaving her first husband, was living with the applicant.

It is argued that since there was no marriage between the applicant and the deceased,
no offence under Section 304 B I.P.C. is made out.
Further it is argued that the deceased committed suicide due to depression when the financial condition of the applicant became very poor during lockdown.

It is further argued that even the post mortem examination report of the deceased is suggestive of commission of suicide as the doctor has found single ligature mark on the body of the deceased and cause of death has been opined as asphyxia due to ante mortem hanging.
It is further argued that the applicant could not fulfil the desires of the deceased due to financial crisis and as such she was under stress and mental depression and committed suicide.
It is argued that charge sheet in the matter has been submitted against the applicant only whereas his father and brother who were named in the F.I.R. have been exonerated by the police.
The applicant is having no criminal history as stated in para-29 of the affidavit and is in jail since 16.9.2020.
Per contra, learned State counsel opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The case of the prosecution is specific to the fact that the applicant and the deceased had solemnized love marriage.
The First Informant Report states of both of them marrying each other.
Further the first informant even in his statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that the applicant and the deceased had married each other.
It is argued that even otherwise the case of the applicant is that the deceased was living with him.
In para-18 of the affidavit it is admitted by the applicant that the deceased was living with him.
It is argued that since the deceased was living with the applicant the applicant was under burden to explain the death of the deceased in his house while living with him.
It is argued that there is no plausible explanation given by the applicant regarding death of the deceased.
After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that the prosecution case is of the applicant and the deceased marrying each other.

There is an admission by the applicant that he was living with the deceased at Satish Seth @ Satish Soni vs State Of U.P. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92001087/
3 the time of incident.

sentences.text: There is no plausible explanation given as to why the deceased has committed suicide.
Looking to fact and circumstances of the case, nature of evidence and gravity of offence, I do not find it a fit case to release the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is rejected."
9. The trial in the matter is going on in which three witnesses have already been examined.

In so far as the argument with regards to the fact that door of the room was locked from inside and the same was broken and the deceased was found hanging, is a matter of appreciation of evidence which can be done by the trial court at the appropriate stage.
There is no new and fresh ground to release the applicant on bail.
10. The third bail application is, accordingly, rejected.
